{"id": "975faf9c-e85c-4059-adbf-1a5b180a5d6a", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_Us15OuINYmlPwSDQGBQHTr", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Identity and Access Management\",\"context\":\"### Make the EKS Cluster Endpoint private\\n\\nBy default when you provision an EKS cluster, the API cluster endpoint\\nis set to public, i.e. it can be accessed from the Internet. Despite\\nbeing accessible from the Internet, the endpoint is still considered\\nsecure because it requires all API requests to be authenticated by IAM\\nand then authorized by Kubernetes RBAC. That said, if your corporate\\nsecurity policy mandates that you restrict access to the API from the\\nInternet or prevents you from routing traffic outside the cluster VPC,\\nyou can:\\n\\n* Configure the EKS cluster endpoint to be private. See\\n Modifying\\n Cluster Endpoint Access for further information on this topic.\\n* Leave the cluster endpoint public and specify which CIDR blocks can\\n communicate with the cluster endpoint. The blocks are effectively a\\n whitelisted set of public IP addresses that are allowed to access the\\n cluster endpoint.\\n* Configure public access with a set of whitelisted CIDR blocks and set\\n private endpoint access to enabled. This will allow public access from a\\n specific range of public IPs while forcing all network traffic between\\n the kubelets (workers) and the Kubernetes API through the cross-account\\n ENIs that get provisioned into the cluster VPC when the control plane is\\n provisioned\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/identity-and-access-management.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) controls\",\"context\":\"## [CT.EKS.PR.1] Require an Amazon EKS cluster to be configured with public access disabled to the cluster Kubernetes API server endpoint\\n\\nThis control checks whether an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) cluster endpoint disallows public access to the cluster Kubernetes API server endpoint.\\n\\n* **Control objective:** Limit network access\\n* **Implementation:** CloudFormation guard rule\\n* **Control behavior:** Proactive\\n* **Resource types:** `AWS::EKS::Cluster`\\n* **CloudFormation guard rule:**\\n CT.EKS.PR.1 rule specification\\n\\n**Details and examples**\\n\\n* For details about the PASS, FAIL, and SKIP behaviors associated with\\n this control, see the:\\n CT.EKS.PR.1 rule specification\\n* For examples of PASS and FAIL CloudFormation templates related to\\n this control, see:\\n CT.EKS.PR.1 example templates\\n\\n**Explanation**\\n\\nWhen you create a new cluster, Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) creates an endpoint for the managed Kubernetes API server, which you can use to communicate with your cluster using Kubernetes management tools, such as `kubectl`. By default, this API server endpoint is public to the internet, and access to the API server is secured using a combination of AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) along with native Kubernetes Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Enabling private access to the Kubernetes API server ensures that all communication between your nodes and the API server stays within your VPC. You can limit the IP addresses that have access to your API server from the internet, or you can completely disallow internet access to the API server\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/eks-rules.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Configuring control plane egress routing\",\"context\":\"## IAM condition key\\n\\nAmazon EKS supports the `eks:controlPlaneEgressMode` condition key. You can use this key in IAM policies or service control policies (SCPs) to control which egress mode callers can specify when they create or update clusters.\\n\\nThe condition key applies to the following actions:\\n\\n* `eks:CreateCluster`\\n* `eks:UpdateClusterConfig`\\n\\nFor example, the following SCP denies cluster creation and configuration updates unless the caller specifies `CUSTOMER_ROUTED`:\\n\\n```\\n{\\n \\\"Version\\\": \\\"2012-10-17\\\",\\n \\\"Statement\\\": [\\n {\\n \\\"Sid\\\": \\\"RequireCustomerRoutedControlPlane\\\",\\n \\\"Effect\\\": \\\"Deny\\\",\\n \\\"Action\\\": [\\n \\\"eks:CreateCluster\\\",\\n \\\"eks:UpdateClusterConfig\\\"\\n ],\\n \\\"Resource\\\": \\\"*\\\",\\n \\\"Condition\\\": {\\n \\\"StringNotEquals\\\": {\\n \\\"eks:controlPlaneEgressMode\\\": \\\"CUSTOMER_ROUTED\\\"\\n }\\n }\\n }\\n ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\nUse this policy to enforce that all new and updated clusters in your organization use the `CUSTOMER_ROUTED` egress mode\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/control-plane-egress.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up CIS EKS Benchmark 5.4.1 and 5.4.2 wording"}
